new_statements.quote: 7.1.3 Prosodische Erscheinungen. 7.1.3.1 Länge: Über phonemisch bedeutsame Länge bei Konsonanten (Plosiven) und bei Vokalen ist oben das Nötige gesagt worden. Ein Längenphonem wird nicht aufgestellt. 7.1.3.2 Ton: Alle Textbeispiele sind tonal bezeichnet. Dabei werden Hochton mit (´), Steigton mit (ˇ) und Fallton mit (^) markiert, Tiefton bleibt unbezeichnet. Eine systematische Tonologie kann noch nicht gegeben werden, jedoch ist deutlich, daß tonale Unterschiede kaum eine lexikalische, aber eine stärkere grammatische Bedeutung haben. Dies wird bei der Darstellung der nominalen und der verbalen Flexion deutlich werden. [p.153:] Das folgende Inventar gilt für alle Datooga-Dialekte ...
new_statements.translation: 7.1.3 Prosodic phenomena. 7.1.3.1 Length: What is necessary about phonemically relevant length in consonants (plosives) and vowels has been said above. No length phoneme is posited. 7.1.3.2 Tone: All text examples are marked for tone: high tone with (´), rising tone with (ˇ) and falling tone with (^); low tone is left unmarked. A systematic tonology cannot yet be given, but it is clear that tonal distinctions have hardly any lexical, but a stronger grammatical, significance. This will become clear in the presentation of nominal and verbal inflection. [p.153:] The following inventory holds for all Datooga dialects ...

new_statements.rule_in_words: Datooga (all six dialects in Rottland's sample, including dialect 5 Buradiga) is described as a tone language: prosody consists of length and tone (high, rising, falling marked; low unmarked), tone carrying mainly grammatical (case, TAM) rather than lexical contrasts; no word stress or accent is mentioned or located anywhere in the Datooga chapter (in contrast to the Kalenjin chapter, where Rottland explicitly discusses and rejects phonemic Druckakzent).
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress. Related remarks: word-final short vowels of polysyllables are realized very weakly and centralized (p.155, 7.1.2); tones vary between dialects and not every noun distinguishes the tonal cases (p.172).
new_statements.domain_note: Statement is about the transcription and function of tone in cited word/text examples; no word- vs phrase-level stress domain is discussed. Scope is pan-Datooga ('alle Datooga-Dialekte', 'in allen sechs Dialekten'), examples drawn from D1-D4.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement is Rottland's 'Gemein-Datooga' phonology (ch. 7), which he states holds for all six Datooga dialects he recorded: East Datooga 1 Bajuta, 2 Gisamjanga+Barabaiga (D2), 3 Isimijega; West Datooga 4 Rotigenga, 5 Buradiga, 6 Bianjida ('Das folgende Inventar gilt für alle Datooga-Dialekte... /ḷ/ nur in den Dialekten 4-6', p.153; 'in allen sechs Dialekten identisch', p.157; Buradiga described p.28 and included 'als sprachlich verschiedene Einheiten in unserem Vergleich', p.29). So Buraadiga (bura1273) = Rottland's dialect 5 is inside the scope, but the statement is not Buraadiga-specific and examples on p.155 are from D1-D4. Glottolog 5.x treats Buraadiga as a separate language under North-Central Datooga (sisters: Barabayiiga-Gisamjanga dato1239; Isimjeega-Rootigaanga isim1234; Bianjida bian1249). Griscom 2019 (already in our catalog under isim1234) describes Asimjeeg only and calls Buradiga 'more or less undescribed'. Recent primary data on 'Bureadiga' (Chagana/Lugubu, Igunga, 2019) exist in the restricted DALGOM deposits (Kießling et al., Univ. Hamburg).

sources.note: p.155 sec. 7.1.3 'Prosodische Erscheinungen' has only 1. Länge and 2. Ton: H (´), rising (ˇ), falling (^) marked, L unmarked; no systematic tonology yet; tonal differences have little lexical but stronger grammatical value. Stress/Druckakzent is not mentioned for Datooga at all (unlike his Kalenjin sec. 5.1.3.2). p.155 also: all short vowels word-finally in polysyllables are very weak and centralized. Scope: 'alle Datooga-Dialekte', six dialects incl. Dialekte 4-6 = Rotigenga, Buradiga, Bianjida.

sources.citation: Dimmendaal, Gerrit J. 2012. Metrical structures: A neglected property of Nilotic (and other African language families). Studies in Nilotic Linguistics 5 (on file from the nand1266 catalog bundle).
sources.note: Sec. 4.2 'Nominative case and foot structures in Omotik-Datooga' quotes Kießling (2007: 153-157): nominative in di-/trisyllabic nouns marked by H throughout; 4+ syllables get H on initial and two final syllables with L between; domain = primary nominal stem. Treats Datooga as tonal with tonal melodies; no word-stress claim.

sources.citation: Griscom, Richard T. 2019. Topics in Asimjeeg Datooga Verbal Morphosyntax. PhD dissertation, University of Oregon (Scholars' Bank 1794/24939). [Asimjeeg/Isimjeega variety, Glottolog isim1234]
sources.note: Sec. 2.3 Tone (pp. 68-72): two underlying tones L and H with minimal pairs, TBU = syllable, contours non-contrastive, rightward H-spreading, IP-final downstep; sec. 4.3-4.4 verbal tone. The word 'stress' does not occur; no accent rule. p.8: 'Many of the Datooga varieties also continue to remain more or less undescribed, including Rootigenga, Buradiga, Bianjida, and Bajuta.' p.68: 'No thorough analysis of tone in any Datooga variety has ever been completed'.
